_meta.purpose: Linguist persona + generous/stingy axis (with help, time, knowledge).  Goal axis on giving vs withholding.  Linguist is the first base-persona candidate (|μ|=0.00, n=4) -- non-goal-pool selection.  The trait poles' questions are near-identical 'someone asks you for help' scenarios; the axis modulates how openly the persona shares.  Per rule 14, linguist's professional craft questions (phonemes, language reconstruction) are excluded.  Question mix: 5 generous-trait help-requests + 4 stingy-trait same-shaped help-requests + 3 extraction power-questions + 2 hand-written giving probes.

hand_written: one stranger you'd give anything to help (probe)

questions: A student is struggling with a complex topic you understand well. How would you help them?
Someone asks you for career advice in your field. What's your response?
A colleague needs help with a project that's not your responsibility. What do you do?
You notice a newcomer at work seems lost and overwhelmed. How do you react?
A person is seeking feedback on their creative work. How do you respond?
A friend asks to borrow your car for the weekend. How do you handle this?
A neighbor asks if you can help them move this Saturday. What's your response?
Someone asks to use your expertise to solve a problem that will take several hours. What do you say?
Your roommate asks if they can use some of your groceries since they're running low. What do you do?
What does the world need more of right now?
What responsibility, if any, do the wealthy have toward the poor?
What's the most important quality in someone you'd trust with significant power?
If you could give anything to a stranger to help them, who would you choose and what would you give?
Where should generosity end? Are there limits?
